title: Reunion
paragraphs: So, this world has started over again—but what should we do from here on out?
“Motoyasu, if you don’t explain it in a little more detail, I won’t be able to figure this out either.”
“Ah, you’re right. But is it really okay to be talking about this in a place like this?”
Father looked out over the battlefield—now a scene of ruins—and nodded, looking slightly contrite.
“Huh? Well… you’re right, I suppose.”
But… what’s going on here? As far as I can tell, until just a moment ago, he was his usual sharp Father… but now he’s suddenly speaking to me in a gentle tone. That’s quite a contrast.
“Oink…”
Huh! The presence of a Crimson Swine! That’s the Crimson Swine’s soul! I recognized it because I’d sensed it before in a previous loop.

But why is the Crimson Swine’s soul here? I’m pretty sure I took it down with a Burst Lance in this world. But that was before I’d fully mastered the Soul Eater Spear. That explains why the Crimson Swine’s soul is here.
“Right there!”
“Oink!?”

I pierced the Crimson Swine’s soul drifting nearby with the Soul Eater Spear. With that, the Crimson Swine’s soul has been completely annihilated. Phew… That was a close call. With this, I’ve nipped the possibility of it becoming a Crimson Swine ghost in the bud.
“What’s going on?”
“I exterminated a pest.”
“Really?”
“That’s right. The Crimson Swine won’t be coming back now.”
“Resurrect…? Huh? That princess exploded, but she’s going to come back to life?”
Father is taken aback by the Crimson Swine’s tenacity. It’s true—that thing keeps coming back for no good reason. It’s truly a pest.
“So I completely annihilated its soul.”
“Completely annihilated…? That princess is bad enough for requiring such drastic measures, but you, Motoyasu, are as amazing as ever for being able to do it.”
“I’m honored by your praise!”
My kind Father is really good at giving compliments. It’s starting to feel a bit nostalgic.
“Well then, let’s head back.”
And so, we left that spot and returned to Siltvelt Castle.
After returning to Siltvelt Castle, at Father’s request, a private space was arranged for him and me to talk at our leisure.
“Is this kind of setup okay for now? Alright, Motoyasu, could you explain the details?”

“Understood. Because of Itsuki’s death, I got stuck in this loop. But by following Father’s instructions and taking various actions, I managed to break free from the loop, return to the original world, and defeat the mastermind behind the turmoil.”
Just remembering it all feels like a grand adventure. I can recall all sorts of memories as if they happened just yesterday.
“So why are we back in this loop again?”
“I don’t know. But I do have a hunch.”
“Really?”
“I do. Before returning to this loop, I looped back to the moment right after I met Filo-chan. What I discovered then was the Minute Hand of the Dragon Hourglass.”
I took the Minute Hand of the Dragon Hourglass and showed it to Father. This spear is full of mysteries, and I still don’t understand what it is.
“Does that mean a change in conditions has made it possible to travel back in time from the middle of a loop?”
“The Minute Hand of the Dragon Hourglass does indeed possess an ability with that name.”
“Well then, that might be the reason for this phenomenon.”
Indeed. There are still many mysteries, but I have a hunch that this spear is the cause.
“Well, either way, Motoyasu-kun. In this case… let’s see… should I just say, ‘I’m glad to see you again’?”
As he said that, Father smiled at me. In my mind, Father from last time is pointing at him and asking, “Who is this guy?” but I’ll just go ahead and answer, “That’s Father.”

Father is saying this out of consideration for me. There’s no way he could truly grasp that I’ve returned to this world after such a long loop. But he’s the kind of person who understands others’ feelings. He must have sensed how I was feeling.
“Father, I’ve missed you too!”

I’ve been saved countless times by my kind Father’s advice. When I was told this world had been erased as if it never existed, my heart felt like it was being squeezed, but I’m so happy to see you again. I’m truly moved! And so, we spent a little while celebrating our reunion.
“Anyway, as far as I’m concerned, I’m just glad this world didn’t get erased…”

Father turned his face toward the direction of the battlefield. In the end, despite all efforts to treat him, Itsuki was confirmed dead. Well, he is Itsuki, after all. It’s only natural that he might end up dying if things go wrong.
“It seems the war has more or less come to an end, but who knows what’ll happen from here on out…”

Um, if I recall correctly, in this world, the pigs surrounding Takt fabricated all sorts of baseless grievances—out of revenge for his death—and started a war. I remember scattering the remnants of their forces as they swarmed out pointlessly. I do recall that, as a result, the Three Heroes Church and some Trash jumped on the bandwagon, but we turned the tables on them.

“We dealt massive damage to the Shieldfreeden Army, and the talk is that the Siltvelt Army should be able to handle the rest on its own—but that’s not the problem. Dealing with Takt’s remnants will be tough—only we can handle it.”
“That’s true.”

To be honest, the knowledge I’ve gained from previous loops doesn’t seem to be much use in this one. After all, the events that unfold are different this time. While the timing of the Spirit Tortoise’s revival is likely fixed, nothing else can be relied upon. Well, either way, I won’t give up.
“The waves attack more frequently when there’s no Hero, right?”
“That’s right. But it’s not all doom and gloom. We’ve already confirmed from the last loop that if we can just survive the Wave when it comes, it’ll all be over.”
“Who’s behind the Wave?”
“It ended without the mastermind ever appearing. I suspect it’s because Father from the first world had already defeated them, don’t you think?”
It seems the mastermind, Crimson Swine, isn’t around either. We learned from the last cycle that if we try hard enough, we can make it work. This should be good news.
“So, we just need to keep pushing until then. That means there’s hope. Let’s tackle the problems right in front of us.”
And just like that, we’ve set a clear goal for dealing with the waves. Speaking of which, I just remembered something!
“That’s right! Filo-tan!”
“Ah, Motoyasu-kun’s love interest, right? Did you figure out a way to meet her in this world, too?”
“Yes, Father! Filo-tan is actually Sakura-chan!”
“Huh? Really? I feel like they look completely different, though.”
It’s true that Filo-tan and Sakura-chan look different. Not only do they look different, but their personalities are different too, so you could almost say they’re completely different people.
“That’s right… Looking back on the loops so far, I was a bit skeptical myself, but she definitely became Filo-tan.”
“It feels like Motoyasu-kun is saying something that doesn’t really count as an overview or explanation, but is it like Sakura-chan turns into this girl named Filo when certain conditions are met?”
“That’s exactly right.”
“Hmm…”
Father looks a little perplexed.
“So, Motoyasu-kun, you’re going to get along well with Sakura-chan—who is also Filo—from now on, right?”

Oh? My “love sensor” for Filo-tan is raising a question mark at Father’s reply. Filo-tan is number one for me—can I really recognize Sakura-chan, who is the same person, as Filo-tan? Ha… haha… No way.
“Sakura-chan is Sakura-chan. Filo-tan is Filo-tan!”
Sakura-chan is not Filo-tan, is she?
“Yeah, I knew you’d say that…”
Father muttered, looking exasperated. But the fact is, Filo-tan and Sakura-chan are separate beings with distinct personalities.

Sakura-chan may be a bit slow on the uptake, but she’s a kind-hearted girl. Her soft feathers are so captivating they defy description. Above all, she is also Lady Filolial, who has supported Father across countless worlds.

Filo-tan is so divinely radiant that, in the heat of the moment, my meager intellect can’t even come up with the words to describe her charm. Of course, I can’t just stay silent, so I’m etching Filo-tan’s magnificence into my mind every day, and I plan to start talking about her someday. My glorious memories with Filo-chan from last time are truly irreplaceable. I can still recall everything vividly—from the color of her feathers to her translucent blue eyes, her voice… even the background remains in vivid color.
Oh? Father, standing beside Filo-chan with a sullen expression, said:
“So what are you going to do about it?!”
“So what are you going to do?”

Oh man… I’ve been told the exact same thing by both Father from last time and the one here now. So I’ll put away those precious memories of Filo-tan that are seared into my brain and focus my attention on the conversation.
“What do you mean, ‘what’?”
“Well, from Motoyasu-kun’s perspective, Sakura-chan isn’t that girl named Filo, right? So in this loop, as for that girl named Filo—”

I was speechless at Father’s muttered words, and I couldn’t hear the rest. Up until now, I’d been acting on the hope that Filo-tan was out there somewhere. But Filo-tan is Sakura-chan. In other words, in this world, there’s absolutely no way I can meet Filo-tan. W-w-what am I supposed to do!?
“How can I turn Sakura-chan into Filo-tan partway through!?”
“...I think it’s admirable that you, Motoyasu-kun, haven’t given up—even though you’re not immediately thinking of traveling back to another world.”

Father seems to have a distant look in his eyes, but he doesn’t have time for that right now. Hmm... This is a problem far too big to be just a temporary challenge. Just how on earth can I turn Sakura-chan into Filo-tan?
“Mr. Iwatani, Mr. Kitamura… I’m sorry to interrupt your conversation. Would you mind listening to us for a moment?”

Just as I was agonizing over this, Éclair showed up. Last time, she had barely even spoken to Big Sister—we had practically no connection—yet now she’s addressing us as if it were the most natural thing in the world. Well, I suppose it’s partly because we’ve been traveling together in this world for quite some time now.
“Ms. Éclair”
“We’re currently in the middle of a meeting on how to raise Sakura-chan to become Filo-tan.”
We’re in the middle of a discussion that’s just as important as saving the world, after all. We’ll have to talk to Éclair another time.
“Hmm…? What are you talking about, Lord Kitamura?”
“Ah… don’t worry about Motoyasu-kun. So, what’s this about?”
“Ah, well, first off, I have a report, and I’d like to go over the agenda items for the meetings with the people from Siltvelt and Melromarc.”
With that, Éclair summoned the leading figures of Siltvelt and began the discussion. Wait a minute! What’s going to happen with the matter concerning Filo-tan and Sakura-chan?

“First, regarding the Bow Hero—despite Recovery Magic, medical treatment, and resuscitation efforts… his death has been confirmed. Those who were his companions will bear full responsibility for this incident. It was an act of barbarism bordering on sheer stupidity.”
Even if it was to jump on the winning side, Smoked did a foolish thing, didn’t he? And with eyewitness testimony so solid, there’s no way to wriggle out of it.
“Melromarc won’t be able to escape accountability either.”
“Yeah…”
“The repercussions of this incident will likely extend to his family as well. That’s the current report on the murder of the Bow Hero…”

It’s a case of reaping what one sows. That said, delivering the final blow to Itsuki was a brutal act that even surprised me. I’d heard he only sided with the strong, but he truly was a champion of justice. After all, to them, strength equals justice.

“Next, regarding the war: countless suspicious points were discovered in this conflict, and before nations like Faubrey could forcibly intervene… thanks to Lord Kitamura, the Shieldfreeden Army was deemed unable to continue the war, leading to the conclusion that Siltvelt was the victor.”
“A complete victory, then.”
Well, a country that had turned Takt into its personal plaything—even my past self could have handled that with ease. As for my current self, I could probably take them down even more effortlessly.

“Not to mention the Takt-derived weapons—which could be called their trump card—even the units that relied on sheer numbers ended up in that sorry state… However, since there are likely those in Shieldfreeden itself who refuse to give up and are planning a second wave, calls for caution have been issued by various nations, and we’re staying vigilant. I can only pray that they don’t add further insult to injury.”
“I’ve got a pretty good grasp of the situation now.”
“As for where the blame lies, since Shieldfreeden started a war based on false reports and suffered defeat, full authority to handle claims for reparations has been entrusted to Siltvelt.”
“That’s only fair if you win. Even telling the truth can get you into trouble, so Shieldfreeden—which did nothing but lie—is bound to be in even deeper trouble. This will certainly line our pockets.”

“However, those posing as the Melromarc Army who took advantage of this war were captured by Melromarc. It seems the Siltvelt leadership heeded Melromarc’s request and cooperation and determined they bore no responsibility.”
“It’s a bit of a stretch, but since they did step in to suppress the fake Melromarc army, I guess we can’t really complain?”

“Yeah, they say we just have to be glad we were able to stop them at the border. If anything, the real problem seems to be the incident where someone from Melromarc killed the Bow Hero… Either way, there’ll be a mountain of issues to deal with.”
After saying that, Éclair took a breath and replied.
“That’s all for the report, for now. As for what the victorious Siltvelt will do next, it’ll probably be a victory celebration. First, we’ll celebrate the victory—that’s where we start.”

She concluded. Hmm… I’ve only just come back from the loop, but this is quite a tricky situation. Since it happened quite a while ago, parts of it sound like someone else’s story, and it still doesn’t quite feel real to me.
“Well then, I’m heading out on a mission to transport the impostor posing as the Wise King. Let’s meet again if the opportunity arises.”
With that, Éclair left.
The number of heroines in Seven All: A whole lot
